title: Arithmetic and geometric series
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The new point teaches both the arithmetic and geometric series sum formulas together, but each bank point covers only one of these series, so no single point fits without adding a new idea.

draft.title: Arithmetic and geometric series
card: Terms differ by a constant d. With first term a and n terms, the sum is Sn = n/2 × (2a + (n − 1)d).
Each term is r times the one before. With first term a and n terms, the sum is Sn = a(rⁿ − 1)/(r − 1), where r ≠ 1.
draft.remember: Arithmetic adds the same amount each time, geometric multiplies by the same amount. Put n, a and d or r into the right formula.

a.q: What is 4 + 8 + 16 + 32 + ... for the first 6 terms?
a.why: The ratio is r = 2, so S = 4 × (2⁶ − 1)/(2 − 1) = 4 × 63 = 252. The option 256 forgets to take 1 away from 2⁶, and 63 forgets to multiply by a.
a.clue: Each term is double the one before, so use the geometric formula.

b.q: A hall has 15 rows. Row 1 has 12 seats and each row has 2 more than the row before. How many seats are in the hall?
b.why: The seats form an arithmetic series with a = 12, d = 2 and n = 15. So S = 15/2 × (24 + 14 × 2) = 15/2 × 52 = 390. Using 15 × 2 instead of 14 × 2 inside the bracket gives 405, which is wrong.
b.clue: Inside the bracket, d is multiplied by one less than the number of rows.

check.summary: No problems found. Both card examples and both questions work out correctly (252 and 390), and the explanations match.
